title: Three Israelis and volunteers mapped the country and built Waze, which Google bought for more than a billion dollars

trailer.text: Waze, the navigation app that was born as a solution to traffic congestion in Tel Aviv, was founded by three Israelis: Ehud Shabtai, Amir Shinar and Uri Levine.
It began when Ehud Shabtai received a GPS device and decided to write an app for sharing information about speed cameras.
In the early stages, more than 1,500 volunteers mapped Israel.
In 2013 Google acquired Waze, reportedly for more than a billion dollars.
According to a CNBC article, what was once a small Israeli startup had, at the time of writing, more than 140 million monthly users worldwide.

stations.title: One GPS device and an idea

paragraphs.text: Waze was born as a solution to the traffic congestion in Tel Aviv, Uri Levine's home town.
Ehud Shabtai was enthusiastic about a GPS device he had received, and decided to write an app for sharing information about speed cameras.
The company Mapa claimed that he had infringed copyright.
It was prepared to buy the app from him, but not to allow him to use its maps.
Shabtai decided to delete Mapa's maps and create completely new ones.
The 2006 terms of use of FreeMap Israel stated that the project's purpose was to create a free digital database of the map of Israel with the help of the community of users.
More than 1,500 volunteers mapped Israel in the early stages.
Amir Shinar, later one of the founders, started at Waze as one of them.
The map built in Israel took about three years.
It covered 35,126 kilometers.
According to investor John Malloy, in the beginning the founders used game mechanics to draw people to the app.
Waze was founded by Israelis Uri Levine, Ehud Shabtai and Amir Shinar, all of whom had previously worked at Comverse.
Levine credits his success in part to six years of service in the Israel Defense Forces.
At the launch, Levine described the potential for a global revolution originating in Israel.

stations.title: Investors, a month of money, and growth

paragraphs.text: John Malloy of BlueRun Ventures led the original investment in Waze.
According to him, the investors' bet was that the founders could disrupt traditional cartography, and that the timing was right.
According to him, people from the traditional map industry argued over the years that what Waze wanted to do was impossible.
Levine said that in 2010, when they were seeking a second funding round, they had about a month of money left, but they managed to raise capital.
Total private funding reached $67 million.
Noam Bardin wrote that one of Waze's mistakes was the valuation of its A round, which significantly diluted the founders.
According to Malloy, the breakthrough came when Noam Bardin came in as CEO and moved to California.
Bardin said that when he started at Waze it had about 14,000 users.
Bardin wrote that when Google launched free navigation, the Israeli investors suggested focusing on Singapore or Romania to avoid a confrontation in the US.
From 2009, Waze expanded to 4.5 million users in more than 45 countries.
According to VentureBeat in 2012, Waze had more than 15 million users.
According to VentureBeat, its traffic data was reliable enough to power local TV traffic reports.
According to The Next Web, $30 million in 2011

stations.title: Google buys, and the team stays in Israel

paragraphs.text: According to Fortune, Google beat earlier suitors such as Apple and Facebook.
It was reported that a deal with Facebook broke down because Facebook insisted that the Waze team relocate to one of its R&D facilities in Europe or the US.
Waze's leadership reportedly insisted on remaining in Israel.
Bardin wrote that the Facebook deal was supposed to close at $25 per share.
Google and Waze jointly announced that the Israeli company had been sold to Google.
Bardin wrote that an IPO shifts attention to bankers and lawyers, and that they preferred to spend their time with the Waze community.
According to many analysts, Google's motive for the acquisition was to deny Facebook a prize, and not to improve its own app.
One of the conditions the founders insisted on was that Waze would remain an autonomous business unit within Google and would continue to operate from Israel.
Google vice president Brian McClendon wrote that Waze's product development team would remain in Israel and operate separately for now.
Uri Levine said that the company is very proud of its Israeli roots and that he did not foresee moving anywhere else.
Bardin wrote that Google gave Waze independence to grow from 10 million monthly users to 150 million.
Bardin noted that many expected Waze to fail under Google within a year.
During Hurricane Sandy, FEMA used the app to provide information on fuel locations during a shortage.
In April 2020, Waze reported that its users around the world were driving 60% fewer kilometers compared to two months earlier.
In 2013 the GSM Association gave Waze the Best Mobile App award.
On the phone, Prime Minister Netanyahu wished Bardin “mazal tov” and “mabrouk.”
Netanyahu noted that a billion dollars was expected to come into the country soon.

According to the Times of Israel article, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israelis can be proud that one of the most innovative mobile apps, developed in Israel, is fetching the largest amount of money ever for a consumer service.

Malloy said that in Israel there is a long-standing frustration over the absence of a groundbreaking consumer technology company, and that he and his people felt this pressure; according to him, in their eyes Waze was a national treasure of Israel.
According to Globes, each of the 100 employees who had helped to found the company received more than a million dollars.
Bardin moved to Google after the acquisition.
Levine said that Waze was a beacon to the industry, and that many entrepreneurs tell him they want to be bigger than Waze.
In the US, some critics called on the Department of Justice to stop the deal, because it would strengthen Google's dominance in mobile services.
According to a report in TheMarker, European regulators demanded guarantees that Google would not add Waze's user information to its own user database.
The US Federal Trade Commission later decided not to challenge the deal.
The app was criticized for potentially distracting drivers, who must use their phones while driving in order to make reports.
In 2018, Los Angeles lawmakers threatened Waze with legal action over shortcuts that caused congestion on side roads.
Levine responded to the criticism, saying that Waze redistributes traffic to create a better traffic situation for everyone.
A multi-million-shekel partnership and copyright lawsuit was filed against Waze in the Tel Aviv District Court.
The plaintiffs, developers, claim that founder Ehud Shabtai appropriated the project for himself.
The Supreme Court rejected the appeal against the decision not to conduct a class action, but made it clear that the allegations themselves were not groundless.
Waze responded that it comments on legal matters only in court and not in the media.
In September 2020, Waze laid off 5% of its global workforce and permanently closed offices in Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
According to CNBC, Waze also shut down Waze Carpool, a six-year-old carpooling service, in September (the article does not state which year).
Noam Bardin left the company in 2020 in controversial circumstances, after friction over the work culture at Google.
He complained about the culture of political correctness at Google, and argued that Google was not promoting Waze sufficiently in stores.

claims.text: תביעה ייצוגית-שותפותית ושל זכויות יוצרים בהיקף של מיליוני שקלים הוגשה נגד ווייז בבית המשפט המחוזי בתל אביב.
claims.quote: A multi-million-shekel partnership and copyright lawsuit has been filed against popular navigating app Waze in the Tel Aviv District Court.

claims.text: התובעים טוענים שהמייסד אהוד שבתאי נטל לעצמו את הפרויקט.
claims.quote: that Waze cofounder Ehud Shabtai appropriated the project for himself

claims.text: בית המשפט העליון דחה את הערעור על ההחלטה שלא לנהל תובענה ייצוגית, אך הבהיר שהטענות עצמן אינן חסרות בסיס.
claims.quote: but made it clear that the allegations themselves were not groundless

claims.text: ווייז הגיבה שהיא מגיבה בעניינים משפטיים רק בבית המשפט ולא בתקשורת.
claims.quote: We comment on legal matters only in court, not in the media.

claims.text: ווייז פיטרה 5% מכוח האדם העולמי שלה בספטמבר 2020 וסגרה לצמיתות משרדים באסיה-פסיפיק ובאמריקה הלטינית.
claims.quote: Waze laid off 5% of its global workforce in September 2020 and permanently closed offices in the Asia-Pacific and Latin America regions.

claims.text: ווייז סגרה את שירות הנסיעות המשותפות Waze Carpool בספטמבר.
claims.quote: The company also shutdown Waze Carpool in September, a service connecting Wazers with similar commutes to carpool.

claims.text: המנכ"ל לשעבר נועם ברדין עזב את החברה ב-2020 בנסיבות שנויות במחלוקת, לאחר חיכוך על תרבות העבודה בגוגל.
claims.quote: former CEO Noam Bardin left the company in controversial circumstances in 2020, after friction that arose over the corporate culture at Google

claims.text: ברדין התלונן על תרבות הנכונות הפוליטית בגוגל וטען שגוגל לא מקדמת מספיק את ווייז בחנויות.
claims.quote: Bardin also lamented the culture of political correctness at the tech giant, and insisted that Google was not promoting the Waze app sufficiently in stores

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, אהוד שבתאי קיבל מכשיר GPS ליום הולדתו ב-2005 ואז החל לפתח את ווייז.
claims.quote: When Software engineer Ehud Shabtai received a hand held device with a GPS for his birthday in 2005

claims.text: שבתאי הקים עם הישראלים עמיר שנער ואורי לוין את ווייז והשיק את גרסת הבטא בישראל ב-2008.
claims.quote: Shabtai teamed up with fellow Israelis Amir Shinar, now vice-president of research and development, and Uri Levine, president, to found Waze and launch the beta version of the program in Israel in 2008.

claims.text: ברדין לא הקים את החברה; המייסדים הם שבתאי, שנער ולוין שהקימו את ווייז בישראל ב-2008.
claims.quote: That credit goes to Ehud Shabtai, Amir Shinar and Uri Levine who started Waze in Israel in 2008.

claims.text: ווייז גייסה 12 מיליון דולר בסבב A במרץ 2008.
claims.quote: Waze raised its $12 million Series A funding round in March 2008.

claims.text: נועם ברדין, מנכ"ל ומייסד שותף של ווייז, אישר בפוסט בלינקדאין שגוגל הסכימה לשלם 1.15 מיליארד דולר.
claims.quote: A blog post on LinkedIn from Noam Bardin, who is CEO and co-founder of Waze, confirms that Google agreed to a $1.15 billion deal to buy the company.

claims.text: לפי מקורות בחברה, גוגל שילמה מיליארד דולר במזומן ועוד 100 מיליון דולר בתשלומי ביצועים במזומן ובמניות גוגל לעובדים.
claims.quote: Google won, buying Waze for $1 billion in cash, with an additional $100 million in performance payouts in cash and Google stock for employees, company sources said.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, גוגל ישראל רכשה את האפליקציה משבתאי ב-2013 תמורת כמעט מיליארד דולר.
claims.quote: which acquired the app from Shabtai in 2013 for nearly $1 billion

claims.text: הערכות בתקשורת לגבי מחיר העסקה נעו בין 1.1 ל-1.3 מיליארד דולר.
claims.quote: media estimates had varied from $1.1 billion to $1.3 billion

claims.text: לפי גלובס, ב-2023 משתמשים בווייז כ-150 מיליון איש בעולם מדי יום.
claims.quote: which is used by about 150 million people worldwide every day

claims.text: הוקרה: פרס אפליקציית המובייל הטובה ביותר של איגוד GSM, 2013
claims.quote: won the Best Overall Mobile App by the GSM Association in the 2013 Global Mobile Awards

claims.text: ב-2013 העניק איגוד GSM לווייז את פרס אפליקציית המובייל הטובה ביותר.
claims.quote: won the Best Overall Mobile App by the GSM Association in the 2013 Global Mobile Awards

claims.text: רשות הסחר הפדרלית בארה"ב החליטה בהמשך שלא לערער על העסקה.
claims.quote: the FTC will not interfere with the acquisition

claims.text: 1.3 מיליארד דולר
claims.quote: which news provider Reuters said had been sold for $1.3bn, although terms were undisclosed.
